senses.gloss:
Pāman occurs in the Atharvaveda as the name of a skin disease. The derivative adjective, Pāmana, ‘suffering from skin disease,’ is found in the later Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas. Since it is mentioned as an accompaniment of fever, probably a cutaneous eruption or scab consequent on fever is meant.
Foot notes v. 22, 12. Cf. for the reading, Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 261. See also Chāndogya upaniṣad, iv. 1, 8.
taittirīya Saṃhitā, vi. 1, 3, 8; kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, xxiii. 4; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, iii. 2, 1, 31.
Cf. Grohmann, Indische Studien, 9, 401 et seq.; Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 388; Schrader, Prehistoric Antiquities, 421, n.; Bloomfield, Hymns of the Atharvaveda, 450, 451; Atharvaveda, 63.
